title: "Add event" button disappears if "KOrganizer View" is above "KOrganizer" in file associations
line: The Digital Clock's "Add…" button and middle-click now open KOrganizer even when the hidden "KOrganizer View" helper is ranked above it.
explanation: ApplicationIntegration only looked at the single preferred text/calendar handler. When that is KOrganizer's hidden "KOrganizer View" helper (NoDisplay, Exec=korganizer --view %u), the clock either rejected it because it didn't list text/calendar itself, so no calendar app was found and the "Add…" button disappeared, or accepted it and launched the helper without a file. The change (same as Niccolò's open MR !7320) queries all text/calendar handlers in preference order and takes the first that lists text/calendar itself and is not NoDisplay.

commits.message:
applets/digital-clock: Skip NoDisplay helpers when picking the calendar app

Only the preferred text/calendar handler was considered, so a hidden helper
like "KOrganizer View" on top either hid the "Add…" button or got launched
without a file. Use the most preferred suitable handler that isn't NoDisplay.

BUG: 507161

review.text: Clean and idiomatic fix in the right place: querying all text/calendar handlers in preference order and filtering out NoDisplay helpers and inherited-MIME non-calendar apps fixes both the missing "Add…" button and launching the hidden KOrganizer View helper. `services.value(0)` safely yields a null `KService::Ptr` when no matching calendar app exists, and the before/after screenshots and verification cover both failure modes.

reviews.text: Clean and idiomatic fix in the right place: querying all text/calendar handlers in preference order and filtering out NoDisplay helpers and inherited-MIME non-calendar apps fixes both the missing "Add…" button and launching the hidden KOrganizer View helper. `services.value(0)` safely yields a null `KService::Ptr` when no matching calendar app exists, and the before/after screenshots and verification cover both failure modes.

Replacing preferredService() with queryByMimeType() filtered to non-NoDisplay services that list text/calendar themselves picks the first real calendar app in the user's preference order. That covers both cases: the hidden helper hiding the button, and the helper being launched without a file. The change is minimal and in the right place (ApplicationIntegration, which serves both the Add… button and middle-click), and it keeps the existing no-inherited-mimetypes rule. The before/after screenshots and tooltip show both scenarios fixed, and the regression checks (a visible app ranked first, no calendar app installed) are reasonable.
